messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty incident fired: service=router-proxy-usw2 latency_high (alert_id: pd_88233). 90th p95 p99 spikes from 120ms -> 980ms across a handful of dedicated GPUs. auto-suppression=off
Alex: acked. I'm on it, pulling traces and console. tagging @Jamie and @Maya in case it escalates.
Alex: quick look at route logs: a few 503s but very low volume so far. dashboard link: https://console.redwood.ai/teams/prod/routers/us-west-2?range=5m
Maya: seeing a short KV cache warmup surge on dedicated pool d-gpu-12, requests per second spiked x8. Might be new rollout or a noisy model loading pattern.
Jamie: are there customer errors? any dropped requests?
Alex: error rate ~0.25% 5m window, spike aligns with two hosts that had cache-miss floods. No broad customer impact flagged on CS.
PagerDuty: Alert escalated to SRE (policy: 2min ack window)
Maya: running quick query: `kubectl -n dedicated get pods -l pool=d-gpu-12 --sort-by=.status.startTime` shows two pods restarting around the same time. suspect kv warming + episodic CPU/IO on host.
Alex: grabbing recent logs from one pod: ```
2026-03-15T14:02:11Z WARN kv_cache: miss storm - consecutive_misses=1240
2026-03-15T14:02:12Z INFO model_loader: loaded variant v2-quant (size=8G) in 4.1s
2026-03-15T14:02:12Z ERROR router: request_timeout backend=transformer-serve latency=980ms
```
Jamie: ok. short-lived but noisy. What's current autoscaler doing? any thrashing?
Maya: autoscaler briefly spun up 1 extra instance then scaled back down after 30s. We have aggressive downscale (30s) for that shard — could be too eager.
Lin: no customer complaints in support queue yet. product telemetry shows one internal eval job that started ~14:01 — could be the trigger.
Alex: mitigation idea: temporarily pin routing of low-priority workloads to fallback model variant (smaller) so heavy warmups don't hit primary pool. Can we flip a route?
Maya: I can patch routing for eval-job user to model=fallback-small for 10m. Doing now.```PATCH /routing/routes/evals {"match":"user:eval-bot","model":"fallback-small"}```
Alex: done. Also nudged autoscaler downscale to 90s for shard d-gpu-12 to avoid oscillation.
PagerDuty: Incident updated: acknowledged by Alex at 14:03.
IncidentBot: PagerDuty alert pd_88233 auto-resolved (duration 78s) :white_check_mark:
Alex: monitoring. p95 back to ~110ms, errors dropped to baseline. Looks cleared.
Jamie: nice. root cause hypothesis: a scheduled eval job + aggressive downscale created a cold-KV storm and transient CPU/IO that increased tail latency. Low customer impact but noisy alerts.
Maya: followups: 1) increase downscale window for that shard to 120s, 2) add KV-warmup throttle for eval routes, 3) add alert suppression for short-lived kv miss storms under 2min. I'll file tickets.
Lin: preferrable to put a notice for product teams to avoid large eval jobs on prod shards during peak hours.
Alex: noted. handoff: I'm wrapping up and will leave oncall to Jamie in 15m. No customer action required.
Jamie: taking handoff. leaving a short incident note in ops-runbook and closing PD if no recurrence. :thumbsup:
Maya: ticket created: INF-4821 (kv warmup throttling) and INF-4822 (downscale policy tweak).
Alex: thanks all. marking thread resolved in slack. :white_check_mark:
